notes: Baseline of full `koto next` response bodies for a template whose phases declare no instructions (no `<!-- details -->` marker anywhere). Captured from the binary as it stood before any behaviour change in the inline-phase-details feature.
Every sequence runs in its own temporary HOME and KOTO_SESSIONS_BASE, so no session state carries between them and the real session store is never touched.

`stdout` holds the response bytes verbatim, including the trailing newline the CLI writes. Steps whose stdout is not part of the contract under test (`koto init`, `koto rewind`, and the parent tick that spawns a batch child) are run but not recorded; the response they set up is.

Every call sequence the plan enumerates -- conditional-transition arrival, unconditional-transition arrival, directed transition, self-transition, rewind, the `--full` override, `koto init` plus the first tick, and a batch child's first tick -- is expressible in the template grammar and is recorded here. Nothing was omitted. The non-advancing repeat is recorded too, on its own, because it is the response the delivery rule will change and the one the `--full` entry is the counterpart of.
The bodies were also confirmed identical between the debug binary this harness runs and a `cargo build --release` binary, so the baseline is a property of the source rather than of the profile.

One sequence needs comment: two consecutive directed transitions into the same phase are only reachable because `implement` declares itself as a transition target -- the `--to` handler validates the target against the current phase's declared transitions. That is why the template has a self-transition it would not otherwise need.

sequences.description: `koto init` followed by the first `koto next`: the arrival response for the initial phase.
sequences.label: init-then-first-tick

sequences.description: Evidence routes `gather` to `implement` through a `when` clause.
sequences.label: conditional-transition-arrival

sequences.description: Evidence routes `gather` to `relay`, whose sole transition is unconditional, so the tick chains on and the arrival at `implement` is reached unconditionally.
sequences.label: unconditional-transition-arrival

sequences.description: A second `koto next` on a phase awaiting evidence, which does not advance. This is the response the delivery rule will later change.
sequences.label: non-advancing-repeat

sequences.description: `implement` transitions to itself, ending one occupancy and beginning another.
sequences.label: self-transition-arrival

sequences.description: Two consecutive `--to` transitions into `implement`. The second is reachable only because `implement` declares itself as a target. Note the key order differs from the natural-advancement path.
sequences.label: directed-transition

sequences.description: The workflow is advanced past `gather` and then rewound into it; the next response is the arrival.
sequences.label: rewind-arrival

sequences.description: A batch-spawned child's first `koto next`. The parent tick that spawns it is setup; the child's arrival response is the record.
sequences.label: batch-child-first-tick
